claims.text: ``graph_delta`` reached 12/12 on the hand-written corpus in ``tools/gate_discrimination.py`` — but only after two layers were ADDED specifically to catch the defects the first layers missed, and then validated on those same twelve.
claims.why: Referenced file and data not in this chunk.

claims.text: mechanical — AST operators applied to real functions in this repository, not hand-picked incidents, so the corpus cannot be implicitly shaped by what somebody already knew the detector would catch;
claims.why: No mutation generation code present to verify AST operators are applied mechanically.

claims.text: unbounded — as many as you ask for, which turns n=12 into n=hundreds;
claims.why: No generation loop or parameter for count present.

claims.text: marker-free — no "SEEDED DEFECT" comment exists, so the tautology that inflated the first calibration run to 10/12 is impossible by construction;
claims.why: No code in this chunk prevents insertion of marker comments; generation code not shown.

claims.text: deterministic — a seed picks the sites, so a claim is reproducible.
claims.why: No seeding logic present in this chunk.

claims.text: Every mutant is checked to still PARSE. A mutant that breaks syntax is not a defect, it is a typo, and any tool would catch it — counting those would inflate the score for free.
claims.why: No parse-check code present in this chunk.

claims.text: The names match the vocabulary the hand-written corpus uses so the two can be compared.
claims.why: Hand-written corpus not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Every filter here is static and costs no model call.
claims.why: All filters defined are static sets or simple string checks.

claims.text: Each rejection is COUNTED and named, so the filter can be audited instead of trusted.
claims.why: No counting mechanism or named rejection counters are present in this chunk.

claims.text: A mutant here can never be a product defect.
claims.why: The claim is about the effect of skipping these paths; no mutation generation to verify.

claims.text: A changed repr is not a defect worth catching, and mutating one only teaches the detector to fire on noise.
Constants whose value is display text, not behaviour. Changing a log message or a docstring is not a defect; it is a typo with no consequence.
Real incidents in the hand-written corpus were all removals of exactly this kind of code, so a site matching it is worth far more than a random one.
claims.why: Hand-written corpus not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A mutant on a line no test reaches is a GUARANTEED survivor: it cannot be caught by the gate, so measuring it only dilutes the score.
claims.why: No gate or score calculation present.
